steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Comparison involves identifying similarities and differences between texts, considering perspectives, methods, and how writers convey their viewpoints.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: Write about both texts in each paragraph, using comparative connectives to link them.

steps.title: Examiner's Tip
steps.body: You must compare BOTH perspectives AND methods. Use evidence from both texts equally. Spend about 20-25 minutes on this question.

steps.title: Comparison Exam Strategy
steps.body: This is AQA Paper 2 Q4 (16 marks) - spend 20-25 minutes. You must compare BOTH perspectives AND methods. Use an integrated approach: write about both texts in every paragraph, using comparative connectives (however, similarly, whereas, in contrast). Read both texts first and annotate them side by side. Identify each writer's viewpoint, then find 2-3 points of comparison. Examiners reward responses that weave comparison throughout, not those that write about each text separately.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What are the two main things you should compare between texts? | What is the difference between an integrated approach and writing about texts separately? | Name three comparative connectives for showing differences.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Perspectives (viewpoints) and methods (how they convey those viewpoints). | Integrated approach compares within each paragraph using connectives; separate approach writes about each text individually without comparing. | However, in contrast, whereas, on the other hand, unlike.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read both texts and identify each writer's viewpoint Use comparative connectives throughout Write about both texts in each paragraph Compare methods as well as perspectives Quote from both texts equally Look for similarities AND differences Don't analyse language in depth - focus on comparison
